prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/ACA, Medicare, small‑group/employer, short‑term), whether you want in‑person help, and whether you prefer an independent broker or someone tied to one carrier. I can help you find a great match if you tell me more, but here’s how to find and evaluate brokers in Kansas City and what to ask them.

What I need from you to make a targeted list
- ZIP code or whether you’re on the Kansas or Missouri side of KC
- Type of coverage (individual/marketplace, Medicare, employer group, family, etc.)
- Preference for in‑person vs virtual help, language needs, any special health needs

How to find quality brokers/navigators
- HealthCare.gov “Assister” or your state marketplace (for ACA plans) — navigators/assisters provide free help and are familiar with subsidies.
- Medicare.gov’s “Find a Medicare Agent/Broker” tool for Medicare help.
- National broker networks (e.g., eHealth, GoHealth) if you prefer online options.
- Local independent insurance agencies (search Google/Yelp/BBB) — independent brokers can show plans from multiple carriers.
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” directory.
- Your state insurance department (Kansas Insurance Department or Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance) to verify licensing and complaints.

What to look for
- Proper licensing (check state insurance department).
- Experience with your plan type (ACA vs Medicare vs employer).
- Independent broker vs captive agent (independent = multiple carriers).
- Transparent fee/commission disclosure (many brokers are paid by carriers; ask if they charge you directly).
- Clear communication, responsiveness, and good reviews/references.

Questions to ask prospective brokers
- Are you licensed in Kansas and/or Missouri?
- Do you work mostly with individual/marketplace plans, Medicare, or employer plans?
- Are you independent or affiliated with a single carrier?
- How are you paid? Will I be charged any direct fees?
- Can you show me plans from multiple carriers and explain costs (premiums, deductibles, network, out‑of‑pocket max)?
- Can you help with enrollment, claims issues, and plan changes during the year?

Would you like me to find and list a few top-rated brokers or navigators near your ZIP code and coverage type? If so, tell me your ZIP and what kind of plan you need and I’ll pull options and contact info.
